A strong serif name, double warm-grey rules and spacious margins evoke letterpress typography. Keep the paper white and use real text rather than distressed or rasterised lettering.
A type-specimen identity introduces two rigorously aligned columns. Pair a distinctive display serif with a neutral body and use small section numbers as typographic details.
A disciplined Swiss-style grid uses an offset sans identity, red section numbers and clear column boundaries. Preserve reading order and let mobile screens collapse to a single sequence.
An asymmetric identity and a few primary-colour geometric accents create a Bauhaus reference. Confine shapes to margins and use black body text on a plain white field.
A compact serif identity, ruled date gutter and small catalogue-like labels evoke a library record. Keep every entry as ordinary readable text, without fake accession numbers.
A small monospace identity and short, widely spaced section labels create a telegram-like rhythm. The body remains a comfortable sans serif with conventional dates and no forced all-caps prose.
A graceful serif identity and curved green rules suggest Art Nouveau restraint. Keep ornament at section edges and retain a clean reading column with strong contrast.
A warm brown identity rail and rounded display serif reference seventies studio graphics. Use plenty of white paper, plain dates and a neutral body to keep the nostalgia practical.
A sharp geometric masthead, violet keylines and an offset supporting rail evoke eighties modernism. Avoid neon body text, gradients and decorative grids behind applicant content.
A restrained blue perimeter rule and classic personal-letterhead masthead introduce the resume. Use serif headings, compact contact details and an open chronology with deliberate continuation pages.
